'''''Matematicheskii Sbornik''''' ({{langx|ru|Математический сборник}}, abbreviated ''Mat. Sb.'') is a [[peer review]]ed Russian mathematical journal founded by the [[Moscow Mathematical Society]] in 1866.<ref>{{citation|title=The History of Mathematics: A Brief Course|first=Roger L.|last=Cooke|edition=2nd|publisher=John Wiley & Sons|year=2011|isbn=978-1-118-03024-0|page=73|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=wOGh7XPowAMC&pg=PA73}}.</ref> It is the oldest successful Russian mathematical journal.<ref>{{citation|contribution=La revue ''Matematicheskii Sbornik'' dans les années 1866–1935|first=Serguei|last=Demidov|title=Messengers of mathematics: European mathematical journals (1800–1946)|editor1-first=Elena |editor1-last=Ausejo Martínez|editor2-first=Mariano|editor2-last=Hormigón Blánquez|year=1993|language=French|isbn= 9788432308024|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=M42M5wBTwSMC&pg=PA235|publisher=Siglo XXI de España Editores|pages=235–256|quotation=Elle est la doyenne des revues mathématiques russes; toutes les tentatives antérieures relatives à la fondation d'une revue mathématique n'ayant pas été couronnées de succès.}}</ref> The English translation is ''Sbornik: Mathematics''.  It is also sometimes cited under the alternative name ''Izdavaemyi Moskovskim Matematicheskim Obshchestvom'' or its French translation ''Recueil mathématique de la Société mathématique de Moscou'',<ref>[https://www.worldcat.org/oclc/436479559 Worldcat entry for ''Mat. Sbornik''], retrieved 2013-10-28.</ref> but the name ''Recueil mathématique'' is also used for an unrelated journal, ''[[Mathesis (journal)|Mathesis]]''. Yet another name, ''Sovetskii Matematiceskii Sbornik'', was listed in a statement in the journal in 1931 apologizing for the former editorship of [[Dmitri Egorov]], who had been recently discredited for his religious views; however, this name was never actually used by the journal.<ref>{{citation|first=Allen|last=Shields|authorlink=Allen Lowell Shields|title=Years Ago: Egorov and Luzin, Part 2|journal=[[Mathematical Intelligencer]]|volume=11|issue=2|year=1989|pages=5–8|doi=10.1007/BF03023816|s2cid=189883978 }}. Reprinted in {{citation|title=Russian Mathematicians in the 20th Century|pages=67–70|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=BFsnWXkqZaMC&pg=PA67|editor-first=Yakov G.|editor-last=Sinai|editor-link=Yakov G. Sinai|publisher= [[World Scientific]]|year=2003|isbn=9789812383853}}.</ref>

The first editor of the journal was [[Nikolai Brashman]], who died before its first issue (dedicated to his memory) was published.<ref>{{MacTutor|id=Moscow|title=Moscow Mathematical Society}}</ref> Its current editor-in-chief is [[Boris Kashin]].<ref name="mathnet">[http://www.mathnet.ru/php/journal.phtml?jrnid=sm&option_lang=eng ''Matematicheskii Sbornik''] at mathnet.ru, retrieved 2013-10-31.</ref>

The journal is indexed in [[Russian Science Citation Index]].<ref>{{cite web
 |url         = https://elibrary.ru/title_about_new.asp?id=7876&langid=2
 |title         = Matematicheskii Sbornik
 |website       = elibrary.ru
 |access-date         = 2023-09-11
 }}</ref>

== Selected articles ==
Notable articles published in ''Matematicheskii Sbornik'' have included:
*{{citation|first=С.|last=Соболев|authorlink=Sergei Sobolev|script-title=ru:Об одной теореме функционального анализа|trans-title=On a theorem of functional analysis|journal=Mat. Sb.|volume=4|year=1938|pages=471–497|url=http://www.mathnet.ru/php/archive.phtml?wshow=paper&jrnid=sm&paperid=5759&option_lang=eng|language=Russian}}. Translated in ''Transl. Amer. Math. Soc.'' 34 (2): 39–68, 1963. This paper by [[Sergei Sobolev]] introduced [[Sobolev space]]s and [[Sobolev inequality|Sobolev inequalities]]. In 2009, Laurent Saloff-Coste wrote that "there are few articles that have turned out to be as influential and important."<ref>{{citation
 | last = Saloff-Coste | first = Laurent
 | contribution = Sobolev inequalities in familiar and unfamiliar settings
 | doi = 10.1007/978-0-387-85648-3_11
 | location = New York
 | mr = 2508847
 | pages = 299–343
 | publisher = Springer
 | series = Int. Math. Ser. (N. Y.)
 | title = Sobolev spaces in mathematics. I
 | volume = 8
 | year = 2009}}.</ref>

== English translation ==
From 1967 to 1993 (volumes 1–74) the English version was titled ''Mathematics of the USSR. Sbornik'' (ISSN 0025-5734).

Since 1993 (volumes 75–) it has been titled ''Sbornik. Mathematics'' and abbreviated ''Sb. Math.'' (ISSN 1064-5616).

From 1995 the translation has been published jointly by the [[London Mathematical Society]], Turpion Ltd,<ref>[http://www.turpion.org/php/homes/pa.phtml?jrnid=sm ''Sbornik. Mathematics''] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080604111115/http://www.turpion.org/php/homes/pa.phtml?jrnid=sm |date=2008-06-04 }} at Turpion Ltd, retrieved 2013-10-31.</ref> and the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]]. The volume numbering was also changed and now follows the Russian original journal ''Matematicheskii Sbornik''.

== Impact ==
As of 2018, the [[impact factor]] of ''Sb. Math.'' in [[Journal Citation Reports]] is 1.057.<ref>Journal Citation Reports, accessed 2013-10-31.</ref>
Alternatively, mathnet.ru calculates its impact factor for 2018 as 1.089.<ref name="mathnet" />
